name: Tech Team English
lede: You already sit in standups, review specs, and ship features. This pack gives you the words to keep up in English, not just in code.
outcome: The shorthand your product team uses in standups, specs, and launches — so you can join in without translating.
outcomes: Follow a standup without translating every ticket, blocker, and deploy in your head.
Ask sharper questions about specs, acceptance criteria, and edge cases before work starts.
Talk about releases, rollbacks, and tech debt with the confidence of a teammate, not a visitor.

aside.title: Written for the standup, not the textbook.
aside.body: Every term is one you’ll hear in planning or see in a ticket. Definitions stay short, so you can use them the same day.

words.definition: The staged release of a feature to users, group by group.
words.example: The rollout starts with internal users, then moves to everyone.

words.definition: A problem that stops work from moving forward.
words.example: The API key is still my only blocker this morning.

words.definition: To mark an old feature or endpoint as no longer supported.
words.example: We’ll deprecate the old endpoint at the end of March.

words.definition: To release finished work to customers, even if it’s not perfect.
words.example: If tests pass tonight, we can ship tomorrow morning.

words.definition: A version of a product made available to users.
words.example: The release goes out on Thursday after the final check.

words.definition: To put new code onto a server where it runs.
words.example: I’ll deploy the fix once staging looks clean.

words.definition: A bug that breaks something which used to work.
words.example: The login change caused a regression in the checkout flow.

words.definition: A flaw in the code that makes it behave wrongly.
words.example: There’s a bug in the export when the file is empty.

words.definition: A tracked task or issue in the team’s work system.
words.example: I’ll open a ticket for the broken filter and tag you.

words.definition: A short, fixed period in which the team completes planned work.
words.example: That item is too big for this sprint, so let’s split it.

words.definition: The list of work waiting to be picked up later.
words.example: Let’s move the redesign to the backlog until Q3.

words.definition: A short daily meeting where the team shares progress and blockers.
words.example: I’ll be late to standup, so start without me.

words.definition: A team meeting to review how the last sprint went.
words.example: We agreed in retro to stop starting work without a ticket.

words.definition: Small extra requests that slowly expand a project beyond its plan.
words.example: The new dashboard requests are scope creep, so let’s park them.

words.definition: A written description of what a feature should do.
words.example: The spec is still missing the error states for payments.

words.definition: Something the product must do to meet a user or business need.
words.example: That requirement came from legal, so we can’t drop it.

words.definition: A short description of a feature written from the user’s view.
words.example: The user story is clear, but the acceptance criteria are not.

words.definition: The conditions a feature must meet to be accepted as done.
words.example: Let’s add acceptance criteria before we estimate this story.

words.definition: An unusual situation that the main logic might not handle.
words.example: What happens on an empty cart is the edge case we missed.

words.definition: A temporary fix that lets work continue until the real fix lands.
words.example: I have a workaround, but the proper fix needs a migration.

words.definition: The underlying reason a bug or failure actually happened.
words.example: We still don’t know the root cause of the timeouts.

words.definition: To make a bug happen again so you can investigate it.
words.example: I can’t reproduce it locally, but it happens in production.

words.definition: A test environment that mimics production before the real release.
words.example: The build is on staging now, so please take a look.

words.definition: The live environment where real users use the product.
words.example: We found the issue in production before any customer reported it.

words.definition: An urgent fix shipped straight to production to stop an outage.
words.example: We need a hotfix tonight for the broken password reset.

words.definition: The act of returning to the previous version after a bad release.
words.example: The rollback took four minutes and restored the old checkout.

words.definition: A switch that turns a feature on or off without new code.
words.example: Put it behind a feature flag so we can test it safely.

words.definition: Shortcuts in the code that make future work slower and riskier.
words.example: We’re spending this sprint paying down tech debt in billing.
